summary: @or-sdk/queue-manager preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that fires automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases into a temporary directory and then invokes the freshly-downloaded Bun binary to execute the adjacent 727KB file `math_init.js`. Both setup.mjs and math_init.js are heavily obfuscated in obfuscator.io style (hex-named variables such as `_0x...`, a rotating string-array function `WV8StW` shuffling a large `n7gIxM` string table, and per-function dictionary indirection). The payload is executed under an alternate runtime (Bun) rather than Node, so its contents are not reachable from the package's declared entry point and cannot be inspected without running the deobfuscator. A queue-manager library has no functional need for a separate JS runtime or an obfuscated `math_init` blob at install time. This matches the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: a lifecycle hook that fetches an unrelated runtime specifically to execute an opaque, obfuscated payload shipped in the tarball.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
